title: I Love to Steal Awhile Away
description: I Love to Steal Awhile Away in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Phoebe Hinsdale Brown wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 424 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Secret Prayer”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: I love to steal a-while a-way From ev-ery cum-bering care, And spend the hours of set-ting day In hum-ble, grate-ful prayer.

lines: I love to steal awhile away
And spend the hours of setting day
I love to think on mercies past,
And all my cares and sorrows cast
I love by faith to take a view
The prospect doth my strength renew,
Thus, when life's toilsome day is o'er,
Be calm as this impressive hour,

licence: Public domain: Phoebe Hinsdale Brown died in 1861.
credits: Words by Phoebe Hinsdale Brown (1783–1861), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
